source_issues.finding: Word-level/subword/character choice is presented categorically for task/language classes; the translation retains this simplified source rule rather than broadening it into a verified universal claim.

The regex covers ASCII letter runs and ASCII apostrophes; the fallback also emits non-ASCII letters as individual tokens, although prose calls its fallback punctuation. Independently observed café -> caf, é and don’t -> don, ’, t. Code preserved.

The source claims Porter step 1b would fix poni to pony, while the source exercise describes step 1b ed/ing removal and consonant handling, which does not explain that claimed change. This is a source algorithm-description concern; not silently corrected or presented as externally revalidated.

The fallback strips ing without double-consonant handling and checks original-case suffixes: hopping -> hopp, jumping -> jump, JUMPING -> jumping in independent finite tests. Lookup-table normalization and fallback normalization differ.

spaCy morphologizer is named as a lemmatization option; its exact component responsibility needs a separate official-source check. Translation keeps morphologizer and explains it as a morphology-tagging component rather than replacing the API name.
The built pipeline defaults all items to NOUN without a tagger, so running remains running; the limitation is expressly preserved in Chinese.
NLTK resources and spaCy en_core_web_sm are external resources, and nltk/spacy are outside the repository execution allowlist. Reviewer did not install, download or execute these examples.

Comparative speed/accuracy/component-swapping claims, the specific spaCy 2.x -> 3.x contraction example and the most-common-failure assertion are unverified source generalizations; qualifiers and versioned token examples are faithfully retained.
